extraction.name: MathQA
extraction.description: A large-scale, diverse dataset of 37k English multiple-choice math word problems covering multiple math domain categories, densely annotated with operation programs.
extraction.creator: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, and Hannaneh Hajishirzi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Problems from the AQuA dataset were categorized into math domains using term frequencies, and then crowd workers were used to carefully align problems with formal operation programs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Closely similar problems were found using Levenshtein distance with a threshold of 4 words in edit distance, numeric values were replaced with generic numbers, and annotations were expanded to cover more problems from the AQuA dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Math problems were first categorized into math domains using term frequencies. These domains were used to prune the search space of possible operations to align with the word problem text.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were provided with a problem description, a list of operations related to the problem category, and a list of valid arguments. They iteratively selected operations and arguments until the problem was solved. The platform only accepted programs which included some numbers from the problem, and whose final calculation was very close to the correct numeric solution.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotators were dynamically evaluated through quality-control questions. A validation strategy was leveraged where at least 2 out of 3 validators had to rank the operation program as valid for it to be selected. The validation accuracy was 94.64% across categories.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 validators per item (at least 2 out of 3 validators should rank the operation program as valid)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some problems are not solvable given current math word problem solving frameworks because they require a level of reasoning not yet modeled by neural networks (e.g., sequence problems). There are also problems that have multiple interpretations leading to multiple correct solutions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation (dev), and Testing of deep neural approaches to math word problem solving.
